title: Three biases that hurt traders: anchoring, loss aversion, recency
summary: Being a good portfolio manager is often about overcoming human biases. Anchoring: deciding from a past number like your cost basis. Loss aversion: a $100 loss hurts about twice as much as a $100 gain, so traders cut winners early and let losers run. Recency bias: after three wins you size up and get hurt. Be aware of them and look forward.

steps.caption: Many possible equity paths for the same strategy.
The median path. Your edge is the same, whatever happened in the last three trades.
Recency bias: sizing up after a win streak makes these drawdowns deeper.
Anchoring: your cost basis is a past number. It says nothing about the trade's future.
Loss aversion: losses hurt about twice as much as gains. Cut losers by rule, not by feeling.

takeaways: Anchoring on cost basis is backward looking.
Loss aversion makes traders cut winners early and hold losers too long.
Recency bias leads to oversizing after a streak; keep sizing rules fixed.
